title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

lc.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

scenario:
prices[i] is a stock's price on day i. You may buy one share on one day and sell it on a LATER day. Return the largest profit you can make; if no trade makes money, return 0.

Example 1:
Input: prices = [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]
Output: 5
Why: buy on day 1 (price 1), sell on day 4 (price 6).

Example 2:
Input: prices = [7, 6, 4, 3, 1]
Output: 0
Why: prices only fall, so don't trade.

Constraints:
1 <= len(prices) <= 10^5
0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4

Write: def max_profit(prices) — the driver calls it on Example 1 and prints the result.

intro.job:
prices[i] is a stock's price on day i. You may buy one share on one day and sell it on a LATER day. Return the largest profit you can make; if no trade makes money, return 0.

Example 1:
Input: prices = [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]
Output: 5
Why: buy on day 1 (price 1), sell on day 4 (price 6).

Example 2:
Input: prices = [7, 6, 4, 3, 1]
Output: 0
Why: prices only fall, so don't trade.

Constraints:
1 <= len(prices) <= 10^5
0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4

Write: def max_profit(prices) — the driver calls it on Example 1 and prints the result.

idea.rule: You can only sell AFTER you buy — the cheapest day so far is the only buy that matters, then ask what selling today would make.
idea.detail: This is problem 043 (Buy low, sell high) in interview format. The biggest price minus the smallest price ignores time: the 7 came before the 1, so you can't sell at 7 after buying at 1. Walk the days once, keeping the lowest price seen SO FAR and the best profit so far — each day, first update the low, then ask what selling today would make.

watch.code:
def max_profit(prices):
    low = prices[0]
    best = 0
    for p in prices:
        low = min(low, p)
        best = max(best, p - low)
    return best

print(max_profit(prices))

model_restatement: Find the biggest gain from buying on one day and selling on a later day, or 0.

clarify.question: Can I sell before I buy?
clarify.answer: No — buy on one day, sell on a later day.

clarify.question: What if every trade loses money?
Can I trade more than once?
clarify.answer: No — one buy and one sell.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.

why_line: max(prices) - min(prices) is 7 - 1 = 6, but the 7 is on day 0 and the 1 is on day 1 — that 'trade' sells before it buys.

explain.rule: The highest price minus the lowest price is a time machine — it sells on day 0 at 7 and buys on day 1 at 1.
explain.bridge: The 7 comes before the 1. Can a sale at 7 use a purchase made after it?

fix.rule: One pass: low = min(low, p) keeps the cheapest buy SO FAR, so p - low is always a buy-then-sell.

walk.gloss: Start with the first price as the cheapest buy.
